data.name: Pasiel
data.gender_notes: Pasiel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew 'Pesach', meaning 'Passover'. This name symbolizes the deep love and passion God has for His people, as demonstrated through the Passover celebration in the Old Testament. The name Pasiel carries the meaning “Passion of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Pasiel usually hope their child will grow to embody passion of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of God's love and covenant with His people.
data.etymology: Pasiel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Passion of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pasiel total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: פָּסִיאֵל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פסיאל נגזר מהמילה פס, שפירושה נפש. כך, השם פסיאל יכול לציין נפש טהורה. במסורת היהודית, פסיאל הוא שם שהוענק למי שזכה לקבלת העבודה הגדולה. כשם, השם פסיאל נחשב כסמל למי שזכה לקבלת העבודה הגדולה. במסורת הנוצרית, פסיאל נחשב כשם נבואי, שציין את זכייתו של מי שזכה לקבלת העבודה הגדולה.

in_greek.name: Πασιήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: ονομασία Πασιήλ προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη πας, που σημαίνει «πλήθος» ή «ολόκληρος». Η λέξη πασιάομαι σημαίνει «να εργάζομαι» ή «να εργάσομαι». Στη Βίβλο, η λέξη Πασιήλ δεν εμφανίζεται. Ωστόσο, η λέξη Πασιήλ χρησιμοποιείται συχνά σε ονοματολογικές κοινότητες για να περιγράψει κάποιο άτομο που εργάζεται για την απόδοση του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Pasiel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Pasiel a verbo Pasire derivatur, quod significat «laborare» vel «operari». In traditione Christiana, nomen Pasiel utilis est ad significandum quodam hominem qui laborat pro Deo. In historia Ecclesiae Christianae, nomen Pasiel usus fuit ad designandum quosdam sanctos qui laborabant pro Deo.

in_english.name: Pasiel
in_english.long_meaning: The name Pasiel is derived from the Hebrew name Pasiel, meaning 'labor' or 'work'. In Christian tradition, the name Pasiel signifies a person who labors for God. In biblical context, the name Pasiel is not mentioned. However, the name Pasiel is used in some Christian denominations to signify a person who works for the glory of God.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Pasiel' carries significant cultural implications, particularly for those of Christian faith. The 'Pas' component of the name is derived from the Hebrew 'Pesach', which translates to 'Passover'. Passover is a Jewish and Christian holiday celebrating the liberation of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt. This event is also symbolic of Christ's sacrifice and the establishment of the New Covenant. Consequently, the name evokes a sense of freedom, deliverance, and the enduring bond between God and His people.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Pasiel' embodies the deep love and passion God has for His people, as demonstrated through the Passover celebration in the Old Testament. This celebration's true meaning extends beyond the physical deliverance of the Israelites from Egyptian slavery – it is a symbol of the spiritual freedom and salvation that comes through faith in God. In the New Testament, Christ Himself is referred to as the "Lamb of God," connecting His sacrifice to the Passover lamb and emphasizing the idea of spiritual deliverance and the establishment of the New Covenant between God and humanity. As such, the name 'Pasiel' serves as a powerful reminder of God's faithfulness, love, and redemptive power.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Pasiel: From the Hebrew name "Pesi'el," meaning "little rock" or "rocky pass." In Christian symbolism, it could represent the steadfastness and resilience of one's faith, overcoming obstacles like a rock in a stream.

historical_references.reference: Pasiel of Poitiers was a bishop and a leading figure in the Council of Tours held in 567 AD. He played a significant role in the condemnation of the Three Chapters heresy and the reaffirmation of Chalcedonian doctrine.
Paschalis II was a pope from 1099 to 1118 AD. He played a role in the Investiture Controversy by confirming the investiture of Conrad III, Duke of Swabia, and Henry V, Holy Roman Emperor.
